To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
patients are satisfied with the information they receive in community pharmacy, however, they do not receive all information they need, and they do not receive it at the appropriate time.
the majority of participants (50.3% of participants) do not ask for information about the side effects of their medications, and they rely mainly on physicians (72.4%) for information.

patients’ visits to the community pharmacy were mainly for medication acquisition, while the main reason for non-acquisition was that the patient was already aware of the medication, and that patients were more likely to ask about side effects if the medication was prescribed by their physician.

patient’s perceptions and attitude regarding pharmacist counseling in the community pharmacies.
the need for a change in attitude towards counseling in community pharmacies.
the role of the community pharmacist in providing patient-centered counseling.

there are several barriers to effective patient counseling in community pharmacy in UAE.
the pharmacist should provide a comprehensive and detailed counseling to the patient, and the patient should be well informed of his rights for such a counseling.
there is a significant gap in patient’s perception of pharmacist’s counseling and the practice in community pharmacies in UAE.

patients are not aware of the pharmacist’s role in counseling, and they do not know how to ask for it.
